title: About — BetterMapandan.org
description: About the Municipality of Mapandan, Pangasinan, and the Better Mapandan civic transparency project.
body: About About Better Mapandan An independent civic transparency portal for the Municipality of Mapandan, Pangasinan. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "AboutPage", "name": "About Better Mapandan", "url": "https://bettermapandan.org/about/", "description": "Better Mapandan is an independent civic transparency portal built and maintained by volunteers. It is part of the BetterGov.ph initiative to create open, accessible civic information websites for Philippine municipalities.", "mainEntity": { "@type": "WebSite", "name": "Better Mapandan", "url": "https://bettermapandan.org" } } About Mapandan The municipality History Mapandan was created as an independent pueblo on December 28, 1887, through Director General No. 39. After a period of financial insolvency (1905–1908) when it was re-absorbed into Mangaldan, the town was re-established as an independent municipality in 1909 under Executive Order No. 10 by Governor General James F. Smith. The town was named for the abundance of fragrant pandan plants in the area. Geography Mapandan is a third-class municipality in the province of Pangasinan, Philippines. It covers a land area of 32.92 km² and is composed of 15 barangays. The municipality is located in the western part of Pangasinan, bordered by the Lingayen Gulf to the north and the Agno River floodplain to the south. Population 38,228 PSA Census 2024 Land Area 32.92 km² MPDC Land Use Plan 2024 Barangays 15 DILG / Comelec Cultural Heritage Local traditions and community life Pandan Festival Held annually during the second week of April, the Pandan Festival celebrates Mapandan's cultural heritage with street dancing, pageants, and community gatherings. Pandan Festival Town Plaza The historic center of Mapandan's community life and civic gatherings. Town Plaza Agriculture Rice fields and farmland across Mapandan's countryside — the agricultural heart of the municipality. Agriculture History Mapandan through the years 1887–1909 Founding & Early Governance From southern barrios of Mangaldan to an independent pueblo—and back again. Mapandan’s first two decades were defined by the courage of its founders, the fragility of a new town, and the determination to rise again. Read more Before 1887: Southern barrios of Mangaldan Before Mapandan existed as an independent pueblo, the area belonged to Mangaldan. The future municipality consisted of southern communities including Payapay, Baloling, Apaya and Amanoaoac. The movement toward establishing a separate town was initiated by ten local leaders: Antonio Morales, Sabino Prado, Andres Bongato, Ambrosio Calimlim, Valeriano Tamondong, Tomas Aquino, Fulgencio Nato, Filomeno Sarmiento, Jose Lalas, and Florencio Datuin. December 28, 1887: Mapandan becomes a pueblo Mapandan was established as an independent pueblo through Direction General No. 39, Administration Civil No. 169-C, signed by Governor General Emilio Bravo. The new pueblo was initially composed of the southern barrios of Mangaldan: Payapay, Baloling, Apaya and Amanoaoac. The first town center: Torres The first center of the new pueblo was in what is now Barangay Torres. The area had abundant pandan plants and was associated with a church where Fr. Jose Torres served as parish priest. However, the location proved inconvenient—too close to the southern boundary and too far from communities to the north. The center was eventually transferred to an area that had previously been a sitio of Apaya. Much of the land in the new Poblacion was owned by the Aquino family. Leon Hilario Aquino encouraged settlement by subdividing land into uniform lots and making them available to families. 1903: The epidemic An epidemic severely affected Mapandan, causing major population depletion, residents leaving the town, declining municipal resources, and a financial crisis. The 1903 census recorded Mapandan’s population at 4,198. 1905–1908: Return to Mangaldan Because of the population and financial problems caused by the epidemic, Mapandan was temporarily returned to its mother municipality, Mangaldan. 1909: Restoration Mapandan was formally re-established as a municipality under Executive Order No. 10, signed by Governor General James F. Smith. 1910s–1940s Agricultural Growth & Wartime After its restoration, Mapandan developed as a predominantly agricultural community. Farming remained central to the local economy, with rice becoming the municipality’s principal crop. The decades ahead would bring war, occupation, and the beginning of reconstruction. Read more Agricultural foundations Rice became the municipality’s principal crop and livestock raising developed as an important secondary livelihood. The municipality’s current seal still reflects these agricultural foundations through its rice, cattle, chicken and hog imagery. 1940s: War, occupation and rebuilding The Second World War interrupted the development of communities across Pangasinan. In the postwar years, Mapandan’s communities entered a period of reconstruction and social and economic change. The decades following the war also brought changes in landholding, agriculture, education and local community organization. 1940s–1970s Post-War Community Development After the war, Mapandan’s communities began to take shape. New barangays were formed, land ownership changed hands, and the municipality entered a period of organized community development. Read more Barangays begin taking shape Instead of only telling municipal history, the history of how Mapandan’s communities formed tells an equally important story. Sta. Maria — Formerly part of Luyan, developed from former hacienda land. Tenants gained opportunities to own the land they had been farming after the war. It became a separate barrio in 1965. Golden — Formerly Amanoaoac North, a sitio of Amanoaoac. Its name was associated with the Golden Distillery, which operated after liberation. Golden became a separate barangay in 1967. Torres — The first seat of Mapandan, which once contained several sitios that later developed into separate barangays. 1967–1973: Community development Golden was officially approved as a separate barangay in 1967. The community then underwent substantial development including road improvement, waterworks, school construction, sports facilities, cooperative organization, agricultural training, and sanitation programs. 1972 — Golden was recognized as a SEATO/PACD Model Village, receiving a national-level award presented in Malacañang on September 8, 1972. 1972–1973 — Coral became a barangay through Municipal Council Resolution No. 87 (May 4, 1972), Provincial Board Resolution No. 155 (August 10, 1972), and Proclamation No. 11 (April 25, 1973), followed by a special election for barangay officials on May 6, 1973. 1980s–2001 Modernization Mapandan’s population grew substantially, its services expanded, and infrastructure developed. The municipality moved from historical survival toward economic growth. Read more Population growth Mapandan’s population grew steadily through the second half of the 20th century: 20,094 in 1980, 25,622 in 1990, and 30,775 in 2000. Infrastructure and services The municipality expanded roads, schools, health facilities, and public services. Community organizations grew alongside the population. 2002–2024 21st Century Development From a new municipal classification to healthcare expansion and digital government—Mapandan enters the 21st century with growing services, cultural pride, and a more connected community. Read more 2002: A new municipal classification Mapandan was elevated to a third-class municipality. The municipality credits then-Mayor Jose Ferdinand Z. Calimlim Jr. with spearheading income and revenue-generation strategies that contributed to the municipality’s elevation. 2010s: Celebrating the Pandan heritage The Pandan Festival developed into an important annual celebration of Mapandan’s identity, culture and community. The 9th Pandan Festival was held alongside the town fiesta from March 11–19, 2018. 2017–2018: Early digital government efforts The municipal government began developing an online presence that made government information, public notices, disaster information and community announcements accessible through the web. 2022–2024: Expanding healthcare access National health infrastructure funding supported the development of the Mapandan Super Health Center. The 2022 General Appropriations Act included ₱6.5 million for the project. Its first phase was inaugurated on March 15, 2024, expanding access to laboratory, dental and primary healthcare services for residents of Mapandan and nearby communities. 2020s: Government services go digital Mapandan’s government information infrastructure increasingly incorporates digital channels, including information and access guidance for the national eGovPH platform. 2024: Mapandan today More than 130 years after its establishment as a pueblo, Mapandan is a 15-barangay municipality with a population of 38,228. Its history has been shaped by migration, agriculture, community organization, local government, cultural traditions and continuing investment in public services. ← 1 / 5 → Source: Mayor Karl Vega, “History of Mapandan” — YouTube Sources & Historical Notes Historical accounts drawn from municipal archives, provincial records, and published heritage studies of Pangasinan. Municipality of Mapandan — Municipal Profile Municipality of Mapandan — Physical Characteristics Philippine Statistics Authority — Mapandan PSGC Philippine News Agency — Super Health Center Inauguration Population Growth Mapandan through the census Population by census year Year Population 1903 4,198 1918 6,049 1939 7,286 1948 9,836 1960 13,065 1970 16,653 1980 20,094 1990 25,622 2000 30,775 2010 34,439 2020 38,058 2024 38,228 Source: Philippine Statistics Authority, Census of Population (1903–2024) About the Project What is Better Mapandan? Better Mapandan is an independent civic transparency portal built and maintained by volunteers. It is part of the BetterGov.ph initiative to create open, accessible civic information websites for Philippine municipalities. Our Mission To make government information accessible, understandable, and actionable for every Mapandan resident. We believe that open data strengthens democracy and empowers communities to participate meaningfully in local governance. How It Works We compile publicly available government data — from COA audit reports, PSA census data, municipal disclosures, and provincial issuances — into a single, easy-to-navigate website. Every piece of information is sourced and attributed. Open Source The source code is publicly available. Developers can contribute, audit, and improve the platform. View on GitHub → Independent Better Mapandan is an independent civic transparency portal. It is not an official government website and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or operated by the Municipality of Mapandan or any government agency. Volunteer-Run Built and maintained entirely by volunteers. No government funding is used. Cost to the people of Mapandan: ₱0. Contribute Get involved Better Mapandan thrives on community participation. Here's how you can help: Report Incorrect Information Spotted an error? Help us keep the data accurate by reporting mistakes. Report an error → Contribute Code Developers can contribute features, fix bugs, or improve accessibility on GitHub. Fork on GitHub → Verify Data Help verify government information by cross-referencing with official sources. Submit verification → Share with Residents Spread the word about Better Mapandan so more residents can access government information. Disclaimer Important notice Better Mapandan is an independent civic transparency portal. It is not an official government website and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or operated by the Municipality of Mapandan or any government agency. Information presented on this site is compiled from publicly available government sources and community research. While we strive for accuracy, we cannot guarantee the completeness or timeliness of all data. For official government information, please visit mapandan.gov.ph or contact the municipal government directly.

Covering 32.92 square kilometres, around three-quarters of its land supports agriculture — mainly rice, alongside corn, livestock, and seasonal vegetables. The municipal administration operates under the tagline “Kaakibat niyo ang Aktibo at Responsableng Liderato” (Partnering with you in Active and Responsible Leadership). 01 Founded Dec. 28, 1887 Separated from Mangaldan as an independent pueblo under Governor General Emilio Bravo, led by ten local leaders including Antonio Morales, Sabino Prado, and Andres Bongato. 02 Re-established 1909 A severe epidemic forced temporary re-annexation to Mangaldan. Full autonomy was restored via Executive Order No. 10 by Governor General James F. Smith. 03 Agricultural heart Approximately 75% of the municipality's 32.92 km² is dedicated to lowland crop production, livestock, and poultry farming. Leadership Currently in office Hon. title: Accessibility Statement — BetterMapandan.org
description: Accessibility commitment and standards for the Better Mapandan civic transparency portal.
body: Support Accessibility Statement Our commitment to making government information accessible to all residents. Our commitment Better Mapandan is committed to ensuring digital accessibility for people with disabilities. We continually improve the user experience for everyone and apply the relevant accessibility standards. Conformance Status We aim to conform to the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 at the AA level. These guidelines explain how to make web content more accessible for people with disabilities. Measures Taken We have implemented the following accessibility features across the site: Semantic HTML structure Skip-to-content navigation link Visible focus indicators Sufficient color contrast (4.5:1 minimum) Keyboard-accessible navigation Screen-reader-friendly labels Descriptive link text Proper heading hierarchy Accessibility features Keyboard Navigation All interactive elements are accessible via keyboard. Use Tab to move between elements, Enter to activate links and buttons, and Escape to close overlays. Screen Readers The site uses semantic HTML, ARIA labels, and proper heading hierarchy to ensure screen readers can navigate the content effectively. Color & Contrast All text meets WCAG AA contrast requirements. Information is never conveyed through color alone — icons, labels, and text are always provided alongside color coding. Text Resizing The site uses relative units (rem, em) for text sizing. Users can resize text up to 200% without loss of content or functionality. Forms All form inputs are associated with labels. Error messages are descriptive and programmatically associated with the relevant input fields. Tables Data tables include proper header associations ( <th scope> ), captions where appropriate, and are responsive on mobile devices. Known limitations We are aware of the following accessibility limitations and are working to address them: PDF documents: Some linked government documents (COA reports, provincial issuances) may not be fully accessible. We provide HTML summaries where possible. Interactive maps: The Leaflet map is navigable via keyboard but may present challenges for screen reader users. We provide alternative text descriptions and a data table fallback. Third-party content: Embedded content from external government websites may not meet the same accessibility standards. Feedback We welcome your feedback on the accessibility of Better Mapandan. If you encounter accessibility barriers, please let us know: Report an Issue Use our reporting form to describe the accessibility issue, the page URL, and your browser/device information. Report accessibility issue → GitHub Issues Developers can file accessibility issues directly on our GitHub repository. Open GitHub issue →

Major updates happen when new COA audit reports, PSA census data, or municipal financial disclosures become available." } } ] } General About Better Mapandan Is this an official government website? No. Better Mapandan is an independent civic transparency portal. It is not an official government website and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or operated by the Municipality of Mapandan or any government agency. For official information, visit mapandan.gov.ph . How is this project funded? Better Mapandan is entirely volunteer-run and uses no government funding. The cost to the people of Mapandan is ₱0. Hosting and domain costs are covered by the BetterGov.ph initiative. Where does the data come from? All data is compiled from publicly available government sources: COA audit reports, PSA census data, DILG disclosures, BLGF treasury data, provincial issuances, and municipal announcements. Every source is attributed on the page where the data appears. How do I report incorrect information? Visit our Report Incorrect Information page. Provide the page URL, the specific error, and the correct information if known. Our volunteers will review and update the data. Services Government services How do I get a birth certificate? Visit the Municipal Civil Registrar (MCR) at the 1st Floor, Main Municipal Building, Poblacion. Bring a valid ID and the required fee. Processing time is typically 3–5 working days. See the full requirements on the Birth Certificate service page . How do I apply for a business permit? Visit the Municipal Treasurer's Office (MTO) with your DTI/SEC registration, barangay clearance, and other required documents. New permits are processed in 3–5 working days. See the Business Permit service page for full details. How do I get a building permit? Apply through the Municipal Engineering Office (MEO). Building permits require a zoning clearance, architectural plans, and structural plans. Processing takes 10–15 working days. See the Building Permit service page . How do I request a barangay clearance? Visit your barangay hall with a valid ID. Barangay clearances are typically issued the same day. This is often a prerequisite for other government transactions. Data & Transparency Data questions What does "Placeholder" mean on data? Some data is marked as "Placeholder" when the exact figure is not yet available from official sources. We use reasonable estimates based on available data and clearly mark these so residents know the difference between verified and estimated figures. How often is the data updated? Each data section includes a "Last updated" timestamp. Major updates happen when new COA audit reports, PSA census data, or municipal financial disclosures become available. The site is continuously improved by volunteers. Can I download the data? Yes. The Statistics page includes CSV download options for chart data. The Transparency page provides links to source documents. All data is publicly available and free to reuse under open data principles. How can I verify the data myself? Every data section includes a source attribution and, where available, a link to the original document. You can cross-reference with official sources like the COA website, PSA, or the municipal government directly. Contact Still have questions? For government services Contact the relevant office directly. See the Government Directory for phone numbers and email addresses. For this website Report issues, suggest improvements, or contribute on GitHub . For data corrections, use the Report Incorrect Information form.

title: Privacy Policy — BetterMapandan.org
description: Privacy policy for the Better Mapandan civic transparency portal.
body: Legal Privacy Policy How we handle data on the Better Mapandan civic transparency portal. Overview Better Mapandan is an independent civic transparency portal. It is not an official government website and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or operated by the Municipality of Mapandan or any government agency. We collect minimal data and are committed to protecting your privacy. Information We Collect Automatically collected: When you visit Better Mapandan, our hosting provider (GitHub Pages) may collect standard web server logs including your IP address, browser type, referring URL, and pages visited. This is standard server operation and is not used to identify individual visitors. Search queries: The search functionality runs entirely in your browser. Your search queries are never sent to a server or stored. Language preference: If you use the language switcher (when available), your preference is stored locally in your browser and is never transmitted to us. How We Use Information We do not use, sell, or share personal information. Server logs are used only for maintaining the website and understanding usage patterns in aggregate. Cookies Better Mapandan does not use cookies. The language preference is stored using localStorage , which is a browser-only storage mechanism and is not transmitted to any server. Third-Party Services The site loads the following external resources: Google Fonts (fonts.googleapis.com) — for font loading Open-Meteo API (open-meteo.com) — for weather data (loaded only on the homepage) Leaflet / OpenStreetMap — for the interactive map (loaded only on the homepage) These services have their own privacy policies. We do not share any personal data with them. Data Sources All government data presented on this site is compiled from publicly available official sources. This data is already public and is presented here for informational purposes. Changes to This Policy This privacy policy may be updated from time to time. Changes will be posted on this page with an updated date. Contact For privacy-related inquiries, please open an issue on our GitHub repository or use the report form .

Statutory Personnel Services Cap Section 325(a) of R.A. 7160 limits total personnel spending to 45% or 55% of total annual regular income depending on LGU classification. Mapandan has reduced PS from 51% of operating income (CY 2013) to under 42% (CY 2015), ensuring compliance. Simple: 3 days, Complex: 7 days, Highly Technical: 20 days per RA 11032. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "GovernmentService", "name": "Building Permit", "description": "A building permit is required under the National Building Code (PD 1096) and RA 11032. Includes site inspection, zoning and fire safety compliance.", "provider": { "@type": "GovernmentOrganization", "name": "Municipality of Mapandan", "address": { "@type": "PostalAddress", "addressLocality": "Mapandan", "addressRegion": "Pangasinan", "addressCountry": "PH" } }, "serviceType": "Building, Engineering & Zoning", "areaServed": { "@type": "Place", "name": "Mapandan, Pangasinan, Philippines" } } Description A building permit is a legal requirement under the National Building Code of the Philippines (PD 1096) for any construction, renovation, alteration, or demolition of a building or structure. body: Business Permitting & Licensing New Business Permit Apply for a new business permit at the BPLO in Mapandan. Includes endorsement to Engineering, MPDC, RHU, and BFP. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "GovernmentService", "name": "New Business Permit", "description": "A business permit is required for all individuals or entities intending to operate a commercial business within the Municipality of Mapandan. This permit is issued after compliance with documentary and safety requirements and upon payment of applicable fees.", "provider": { "@type": "GovernmentOrganization", "name": "Municipality of Mapandan", "address": { "@type": "PostalAddress", "addressLocality": "Mapandan", "addressRegion": "Pangasinan", "addressCountry": "PH" } }, "serviceType": "Business Permitting & Licensing", "areaServed": { "@type": "Place", "name": "Mapandan, Pangasinan, Philippines" } } Description A business permit is required for all individuals or entities intending to operate a commercial business within the Municipality of Mapandan. This permit is issued after compliance with documentary and safety requirements and upon payment of applicable fees. Requirements Filled up UNIFIED Form / Community Tax Certificate (from BPLO/Treasury Office) DTI/SEC/CDA Registration (from DTI/SEC/CDA Office or Online Application) BIR COR, if available (from RDO Calasiao) Barangay Clearance (System Integrated) Procedure Fill up the UNIFIED form and submit necessary requirements for verification (10 min). BPLO encodes data into the e-BPLS System. BPLO endorses applicant to various offices: Engineering (Occupancy Certificate), MPDC (Zoning Certificate), RHU (Health Certificate & Sanitary Permit), BFP (Fire Safety Inspection Certificate) (44 min). Pay fees and charges at the Treasury Office. Proceed to the Mayor's Office for issuance of Business Permit. Claim business plate and sticker at the Treasury Office (10 min). Individual: ₱5 + ₱1/₱1k; Juridical: ₱500 + ₱2/₱5k. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "GovernmentService", "name": "Cedula / Community Tax Certificate", "description": "The Community Tax Certificate (cedula) computation: Individual — ₱5.00 + ₱1.00 for every ₱1,000 gross income (not to exceed ₱5,000). Juridical — ₱500.00 + ₱2.00 for every ₱5,000 gross income (not to exceed ₱10,000). Interest of 24% per annum from March 1 to December 31.", "provider": { "@type": "GovernmentOrganization", "name": "Municipality of Mapandan", "address": { "@type": "PostalAddress", "addressLocality": "Mapandan", "addressRegion": "Pangasinan", "addressCountry": "PH" } }, "serviceType": "Real Property & Revenue", "areaServed": { "@type": "Place", "name": "Mapandan, Pangasinan, Philippines" } } Description The Community Tax Certificate (cedula) is computed as follows: Individual — ₱5.00 basic + ₱1.00 for every ₱1,000 gross income from business, profession, or property, but in no case shall exceed ₱5,000.00. body: Real Property & Revenue Transfer of Land Ownership Transfer land ownership in Mapandan at the Assessor's Office. ₱150 recording fee, 30 minutes for Assessor processing. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "GovernmentService", "name": "Transfer of Land Ownership", "description": "Transfer of land ownership is the legal process of transferring property rights from one owner to another. This involves updating the Tax Declaration at the Assessor's Office. The transfer may be due to sale, donation, inheritance, or other legal means. Recording fee: ₱150.", "provider": { "@type": "GovernmentOrganization", "name": "Municipality of Mapandan", "address": { "@type": "PostalAddress", "addressLocality": "Mapandan", "addressRegion": "Pangasinan", "addressCountry": "PH" } }, "serviceType": "Real Property & Revenue", "areaServed": { "@type": "Place", "name": "Mapandan, Pangasinan, Philippines" } } Description Transfer of land ownership is the legal process of transferring property rights from one owner to another. The Municipal Assessor's Office (MASSO) records the transfer and updates the Tax Declaration under the new owner's name. The client first secures a tax clearance from the Treasury Office, then submits the transfer documents to the Assessor's Office. The Assessor records the transaction, cancels the old Tax Declaration, and issues a new one. Fee: ₱150 for recording. Requirements Deed of Sale, Deed of Donation, or other proof of transfer Tax Clearance from the Municipal Treasurer's Office Certified True Copy of Tax Declaration (from Assessor's Office) Valid Government-issued ID of the new owner BIR Certificate of Registration (if applicable) Procedure Secure a Tax Clearance from the Municipal Treasurer's Office. Obtain a Certified True Copy of the Tax Declaration from the Assessor's Office. Submit all required documents to the Assessor's Office. Assessor reviews and records the transfer (15 min). Assessor cancels the old Tax Declaration and prepares the new one (10 min). Pay ₱150 recording fee at the Treasury Office. Claim the new Tax Declaration under the new owner's name (5 min). Service Details Responsible Office: Municipal Assessor's Office (MASSO) Classification: Complex Mode: in-person Processing Time: 30 minutes (Assessor recording); full transfer may take 15–30 working days Fee: ₱150 (recording fee at Assessor's Office) Where to Apply: Municipal Assessor's Office, Main Municipal Building, Poblacion Contact: (075) 633-2653 / 0945-114-2515 Source: Mapandan Citizen's Charter Last Updated: August 2025 Report incorrect information Scanned Document Scanned page from the official Mapandan Citizen's Charter listing the requirements, fees, processing time, and responsible staff for the service. Change of first name: ₱3,000 filing fee. Correction of clerical error: ₱1,000 filing fee. Both require 10-day posting, MCR decision within 5 days, PSA processing 2–3 months.", "provider": { "@type": "GovernmentOrganization", "name": "Municipality of Mapandan", "address": { "@type": "PostalAddress", "addressLocality": "Mapandan", "addressRegion": "Pangasinan", "addressCountry": "PH" } }, "serviceType": "Civil Registry & Vital Records", "areaServed": { "@type": "Place", "name": "Mapandan, Pangasinan, Philippines" } } Description Republic Act No. 9048 authorizes the city or municipal civil registrar to correct clerical or typographical errors in civil registry entries without the need for a judicial order. title: Rpt Payment
body: Real Property & Revenue Real Property Tax Payment Pay your real property tax in Mapandan. Basic 1% + SEF 1% of assessed value. 10%–20% discount for prompt/advance payment. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "GovernmentService", "name": "Real Property Tax Payment", "description": "Real property tax (RPT) is an annual tax on the assessed value of land, buildings, and improvements. Basic Tax = 1% of Assessed Value + Special Education Tax = 1% of Assessed Value. Discount: 10% for prompt payment, 20% for advance payment. Interest on unpaid tax: 2% per month but not to exceed 72%.", "provider": { "@type": "GovernmentOrganization", "name": "Municipality of Mapandan", "address": { "@type": "PostalAddress", "addressLocality": "Mapandan", "addressRegion": "Pangasinan", "addressCountry": "PH" } }, "serviceType": "Real Property & Revenue", "areaServed": { "@type": "Place", "name": "Mapandan, Pangasinan, Philippines" } } Description Real property tax (RPT) is an annual tax on the assessed value of land, buildings, and improvements within Mapandan. Computation: Basic Tax = 1% of Assessed Value + Special Education Tax (SEF) = 1% of Assessed Value. Discounts: 10% for prompt payment, 20% for advance payment. Interest on unpaid real property tax: 2% per month but not to exceed 72%. Payment is processed at Counters 4-9 of the Treasury Office. Staff computes the real property tax due (20 min). Pay the required fees (5 min). Receive the official receipt. Staff records in general collection system (5 min). title: Sanitary Permit
body: Health Services Sanitary Permit Get a sanitary permit, health certificate, or medical certificate at the Mapandan RHU. 53 minutes processing time. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "GovernmentService", "name": "Sanitary Permit", "description": "A sanitary permit is required for all businesses that handle food, beverages, or other consumable products to ensure compliance with health and sanitation standards. The permit is issued by the Municipal Health Office (MHO) after an inspection of the business premises to verify that health and safety regulations are met.", "provider": { "@type": "GovernmentOrganization", "name": "Municipality of Mapandan", "address": { "@type": "PostalAddress", "addressLocality": "Mapandan", "addressRegion": "Pangasinan", "addressCountry": "PH" } }, "serviceType": "Health Services", "areaServed": { "@type": "Place", "name": "Mapandan, Pangasinan, Philippines" } } Description A sanitary permit is required for all businesses that handle food, beverages, or other consumable products to ensure compliance with health and sanitation standards. The permit is issued by the Municipal Health Office (MHO) after an inspection of the business premises to verify that health and safety regulations are met. Requirements Valid ID (government issued, employment, school, barangay certification) Laboratory Tests: CBC, urinalysis, fecalysis, sputum exam, Hepatitis B (from RHU Primary Laboratory) Chest X-Ray, PA (from government or private diagnostic facility) Procedure Present official receipt from the Treasury Office. Laboratory examination of urine, feces, sputum is conducted by Medical Technologist (30 min). Refer to other laboratories for X-ray if needed (2 min). Refer result to MHO for interpretation (10 min). MHO does physical examination and interprets result (5 min). MHO prescribes medicines if needed (2 min). MHO signs the certification (2 min). List down certificate number on logbook and release certification (2 min). body: Social Assistance & Protection Disaster Relief Assistance Disaster relief assistance for families affected by calamities in Mapandan. Relief goods and housing repair assistance available. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "GovernmentService", "name": "Disaster Relief Assistance", "description": "The MSWDO provides disaster relief assistance and rehabilitation services to families affected by floods, typhoons, fires, and other calamities. The service includes distribution of relief goods and financial assistance for housing repair.", "provider": { "@type": "GovernmentOrganization", "name": "Municipality of Mapandan", "address": { "@type": "PostalAddress", "addressLocality": "Mapandan", "addressRegion": "Pangasinan", "addressCountry": "PH" } }, "serviceType": "Social Assistance & Protection", "areaServed": { "@type": "Place", "name": "Mapandan, Pangasinan, Philippines" } } Description The MSWDO provides disaster relief assistance and rehabilitation services to families affected by floods, typhoons, fires, and other calamities. The service includes verification of affected families, distribution of relief goods through the Barangay Captain with the BDCC, and financial assistance (ESA) for families whose houses are totally destroyed. The MSWDO coordinates with the LGU, PSWDO, and DSWD Field Office I. Requirements Master list of affected families (from Barangay Captain) Barangay certificate Certificate of Indigency Procedure Report to the Barangay Captain the extent of damage. The Captain validates and forwards the list to MSWDO. MSWDO attends MDDC meeting conducted by the Local Chief Executive. MSWDO receives list of affected families and endorses to concerned social worker. Verification and inspection team (with Engineering, PNP, DSWD) assesses the damage. MSWDO requests and lobbies for allocation of relief goods from LGU, PSWDO, DSWD FO1. Distribution of relief goods through the Barangay Captain with the BDCC. For totally destroyed houses, MSWDO prepares project proposal for ESA funding. Financial assistance (ESA) is distributed to qualified beneficiaries. MSWDO monitors and evaluates project implementation for house repair/reconstruction. body: Agriculture Crop Protection Technical Services Free crop protection services from the Mapandan MAO. Farm inspection, plant analysis, and pest management recommendations. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "GovernmentService", "name": "Crop Protection Technical Services", "description": "The Municipal Agriculturist provides technical and extension services for crop protection, including farm inspection, plant analysis, and recommendations for pest and disease management.", "provider": { "@type": "GovernmentOrganization", "name": "Municipality of Mapandan", "address": { "@type": "PostalAddress", "addressLocality": "Mapandan", "addressRegion": "Pangasinan", "addressCountry": "PH" } }, "serviceType": "Agriculture", "areaServed": { "@type": "Place", "name": "Mapandan, Pangasinan, Philippines" } } Description The Municipal Agriculturist provides technical and extension services for crop protection. The Agricultural Technologist conducts farm inspections, examines plant health, submits samples to DA-RCPC for analysis, and provides recommendations for pest and disease management. Available to registered farmers. Standard fee ₱115, late registration ₱315–₱1,015. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "GovernmentService", "name": "Birth Registration", "description": "Registration of birth with the Municipal Civil Registrar. Covers three pathways: (1) Attending midwife/hilot reports child's birth — requires Marriage Certificate of parents and Mun. Form 102; (2) Unmarried parents — requires Community Tax Certificate; (3) Hospital administrator — requires Accomplished Mun. Form 102. Free for barangays and organizations. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "GovernmentService", "name": "MDRRMO Training, Seminar & Workshop Request", "description": "The MDRRMO conducts training, seminars, and workshops on disaster preparedness, first aid, search and rescue, and other DRRM-related topics for barangays, schools, and organizations in Mapandan.", "provider": { "@type": "GovernmentOrganization", "name": "Municipality of Mapandan", "address": { "@type": "PostalAddress", "addressLocality": "Mapandan", "addressRegion": "Pangasinan", "addressCountry": "PH" } }, "serviceType": "Disaster Risk Management", "areaServed": { "@type": "Place", "name": "Mapandan, Pangasinan, Philippines" } } Description The MDRRMO conducts training, seminars, and workshops on disaster preparedness and risk reduction for barangay officials, community volunteers, students, and organizations. Topics include first aid, basic life support, search and rescue, fire suppression, and emergency response. The requesting entity submits a letter of request specifying the desired topic, schedule, and expected participants. Requirements Letter of Request specifying topic, preferred schedule, and number of participants Endorsement from the Barangay Captain (for barangay-level requests) Procedure Submit letter of request and endorsement to the MDRRMO Office. Staff receives and evaluates the request (3 min). MDRRMO schedules the training, seminar, or workshop (coordination varies). MDRRMO conducts the training at the agreed venue and schedule. Participants receive certificates of completion (if applicable). title: Ldrrmo Rescue Operation
body: Disaster Risk Management MDRRMO Rescue Operation & Emergency Medical Transport Emergency rescue and medical transport from the MDRRMO in Mapandan. Call the hotline for immediate assistance. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "GovernmentService", "name": "MDRRMO Rescue Operation & Emergency Medical Transport", "description": "The MDRRMO provides emergency rescue operations and medical transportation for residents of Mapandan during disasters, accidents, and medical emergencies. The service includes deployment of rescue teams and ambulance.", "provider": { "@type": "GovernmentOrganization", "name": "Municipality of Mapandan", "address": { "@type": "PostalAddress", "addressLocality": "Mapandan", "addressRegion": "Pangasinan", "addressCountry": "PH" } }, "serviceType": "Disaster Risk Management", "areaServed": { "@type": "Place", "name": "Mapandan, Pangasinan, Philippines" } } Description The MDRRMO provides 24/7 emergency rescue operations and medical transportation for residents of Mapandan. During disasters, accidents, and medical emergencies, the MDRRMO deploys its rescue teams and ambulance to respond to calls. The client or a family member contacts the MDRRMO hotline or reports in person. The MDRRMO assesses the situation, deploys the appropriate response team, and provides transportation to the nearest hospital if needed. Requirements No prior requirements needed for emergency response — call or report directly Procedure Call the MDRRMO hotline or report to the MDRRMO Office in case of emergency. Provide details of the emergency: location, nature of incident, number of persons affected. MDRRMO assesses the situation and deploys the rescue team and/or ambulance. Rescue team provides first aid, rescue operations, or medical transportation as needed. Patient or affected individuals are transported to the nearest hospital or safe location. Service Details Responsible Office: Municipal Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office (MDRRMO) Classification: Simple Mode: in-person Processing Time: 30 minutes (response time varies by location and situation) Fee: Free Where to Apply: MDRRMO Office, Main Municipal Building, Poblacion Contact: (075) 600-2564 / 0969-223-6912 Source: Mapandan Citizen's Charter Last Updated: August 2025 Report incorrect information Scanned Document Scanned page from the official Mapandan Citizen's Charter listing the requirements, fees, processing time, and responsible staff for the service. title: Youth Organization Registration
body: Youth Development Youth Organization Registration Program (YORP) Register your youth organization with the LYDO in Mapandan under the YORP. Free service, official recognition and program access. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "GovernmentService", "name": "Youth Organization Registration Program (YORP)", "description": "The Local Youth Development Office (LYDO) registers youth organizations in Mapandan under the Youth Organization Registration Program. Registration provides official recognition and access to LGU support, funding, and participation in youth programs.", "provider": { "@type": "GovernmentOrganization", "name": "Municipality of Mapandan", "address": { "@type": "PostalAddress", "addressLocality": "Mapandan", "addressRegion": "Pangasinan", "addressCountry": "PH" } }, "serviceType": "Youth Development", "areaServed": { "@type": "Place", "name": "Mapandan, Pangasinan, Philippines" } } Description The Local Youth Development Office (LYDO) administers the Youth Organization Registration Program (YORP) as mandated by the SK Reform Act (RA 11769). Registration provides official recognition of the youth organization, access to LGU support and funding opportunities, and participation in municipal, provincial, and national youth programs and activities. The LYDO assesses the application, verifies membership composition, and issues the Certificate of Registration. Requirements Letter of Intent to Register from the organization Constitution and By-Laws of the organization List of Officers and Members with ages (must be 15–30 years old) Minutes of the organization's founding meeting Endorsement from the Barangay Captain (if barangay-level organization) Procedure Submit the letter of intent and all required documents to the LYDO Office. LYDO staff receives and reviews the application (3 min). LYDO verifies the membership composition and constitution (3 min). LYDO prepares the Certificate of Registration (2 min). Receive the Certificate of Registration upon approval (2 min). Service Details Responsible Office: Local Youth Development Office (LYDO) Classification: Simple Mode: in-person Processing Time: 10 minutes (processing); registration valid upon approval Fee: Free Where to Apply: LYDO Office, Main Municipal Building, Poblacion Contact: (075) 696-0831 Source: Mapandan Citizen's Charter Last Updated: August 2025 Report incorrect information Scanned Document Scanned page from the official Mapandan Citizen's Charter listing the requirements, fees, processing time, and responsible staff for the service. title: Assessor True Copy
body: Real Property & Revenue Certified True Copy of Tax Declaration Get a certified true copy of your Tax Declaration from the Assessor's Office. ₱100, 15 minutes processing. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "GovernmentService", "name": "Certified True Copy of Tax Declaration", "description": "The Municipal Assessor's Office issues certified true copies of Tax Declarations for real properties located in Mapandan. This document shows the assessed value of land, buildings, and improvements for taxation purposes.", "provider": { "@type": "GovernmentOrganization", "name": "Municipality of Mapandan", "address": { "@type": "PostalAddress", "addressLocality": "Mapandan", "addressRegion": "Pangasinan", "addressCountry": "PH" } }, "serviceType": "Real Property & Revenue", "areaServed": { "@type": "Place", "name": "Mapandan, Pangasinan, Philippines" } } Description The Municipal Assessor's Office issues certified true copies of Tax Declarations upon request. The Tax Declaration is an official document showing the assessed value of real property for taxation purposes. The client submits a written request with the property details. The Assessor's Office locates the record, prepares the certified true copy, and releases it upon payment. Requirements Written request stating the property location (lot number, block, street, barangay) Valid Government-issued ID Procedure Submit a written request with property details and valid ID to the Assessor's Office. Pay ₱100 at the Treasury Office and claim the document (2 min). title: Assessor Reclassification
body: Real Property & Revenue Land Reclassification / Reassessment Reclassify or reassess your land at the Assessor's Office. ₱700 fee, 30 minutes processing. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "GovernmentService", "name": "Land Reclassification / Reassessment", "description": "The Municipal Assessor's Office conducts reclassification or reassessment of land when there is a change in land use, classification, or other factors affecting the property's assessed value.", "provider": { "@type": "GovernmentOrganization", "name": "Municipality of Mapandan", "address": { "@type": "PostalAddress", "addressLocality": "Mapandan", "addressRegion": "Pangasinan", "addressCountry": "PH" } }, "serviceType": "Real Property & Revenue", "areaServed": { "@type": "Place", "name": "Mapandan, Pangasinan, Philippines" } } Description The Municipal Assessor's Office conducts reclassification or reassessment of land when there is a change in land use, zoning classification, or other factors affecting the property's assessed value. This may be triggered by rezoning, subdivision, conversion from agricultural to residential or commercial use, or other changes. The Assessor reviews the applicable ordinances, conducts inspection, and updates the Tax Declaration accordingly. Requirements Written request stating the reason for reclassification/reassessment Valid Government-issued ID Zoning clearance or land use change approval (from MPDC) Current Tax Declaration Procedure Submit written request, valid ID, and supporting documents to the Assessor's Office. Staff receives and reviews the application (5 min). Assessor reviews zoning/land use changes and conducts inspection (15 min). Staff updates the Tax Declaration with the new classification and assessed value (5 min). Pay ₱700 at the Treasury Office and claim the updated Tax Declaration (5 min). title: Legislative
body: Sangguniang Bayan Legislative Documents A comprehensive database of municipal ordinances, resolutions, executive issuances, and fiscal data — tracing Mapandan's legislative record from its 1887 founding to the present. Framework Local governance & statutory origins Legal Basis The Municipality of Mapandan operates under Republic Act No. 7160 (Local Government Code of 1991), situated within the Third Congressional District of Pangasinan. The Sangguniang Bayan — a unicameral local legislative council — exercises municipal legislative power, presided by the Municipal Vice Mayor and composed of elected councilors alongside ex-officio representatives from the Liga ng mga Barangay and the Sangguniang Kabataan Federation. Historical Origins Originally an agricultural barrio of Mangaldan referred to as balon baley ("new town"), Mapandan was first established as an independent pueblo pursuant to Direction General No. 39, Administration Civil No. 169-C, promulgated by Governor General Emilio Bravo on December 28, 1887. Following population and fiscal losses caused by an epidemic in 1905 that temporarily reverted Mapandan to Mangaldan's jurisdiction, the municipality was re-established under American civil administration through Executive Order No. 10, signed by Governor General James F. Smith in 1909. No. 5, S-2024 Pipeline Legislative pipeline The legislative pipeline under the Local Government Code of 1991. 1 Filing A proposed ordinance is filed with the Sangguniang Bayan for consideration. 2 First Reading Initial reading and referral to the relevant committee for review. 3 Committee Hearing The committee holds hearings and deliberates on the proposal. 4 Committee Report Findings and recommendations are submitted back to the full council. 5 Second Reading Detailed floor discussion and debate on the proposed ordinance. 6 Third & Final Reading Final vote by the Sangguniang Bayan. 7 Mayor's Approval The Municipal Mayor reviews and approves the enacted ordinance. 8 Provincial Review Submitted to the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Pangasinan for legal review under Sections 56 and 57 of R.A. 7160. 9 Posting & Effect The approved ordinance is posted publicly and takes effect across all 15 constituent barangays. Key Distinction Ordinance vs. Resolution Under the Local Government Code of 1991, the Sangguniang Bayan enacts two types of legislative measures: Ordinance A legislative measure that enacts a permanent rule or policy . Ordinances carry the force of law, create offices, levy taxes, or regulate conduct. They require three readings, publication, and the Mayor's approval (or passage by 2/3 override of a veto). Resolution A legislative measure that expresses the sentiment, intent, or opinion of the Sangguniang Bayan on a specific matter. Resolutions are used for internal housekeeping, requesting national action, or authorizing one-time transactions. They require only one reading and are not subject to publication.

body: About About Better Mapandan An independent civic transparency portal for the Municipality of Mapandan, Pangasinan. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "AboutPage", "name": "About Better Mapandan", "url": "https://bettermapandan.org/about/", "description": "Better Mapandan is an independent civic transparency portal built and maintained by volunteers. It is part of the BetterGov.ph initiative to create open, accessible civic information websites for Philippine municipalities.", "mainEntity": { "@type": "WebSite", "name": "Better Mapandan", "url": "https://bettermapandan.org" } } About Mapandan Ang bayan Kasaysayan Mapandan was created as an independent pueblo on December 28, 1887, through Director General No. 39. After a period of financial insolvency (1905–1908) when it was re-absorbed into Mangaldan, the town was re-established as an independent municipality in 1909 under Executive Order No. 10 by Governor General James F. Smith. The town was named for the abundance of fragrant pandan plants in the area. Heograpiya Mapandan is a third-class municipality in the province of Pangasinan, Philippines. It covers a land area of 32.92 km² and is composed of 15 barangays. The municipality is located in the western part of Pangasinan, bordered by the Lingayen Gulf to the north and the Agno River floodplain to the south. Population 38,228 PSA Census 2024 Land Area 32.92 km² MPDC Land Use Plan 2024 Barangay 15 DILG / Comelec Cultural Heritage Local traditions and community life Pandan Festival Held annually during the second week of April, the Pandan Festival celebrates Mapandan's cultural heritage with street dancing, pageants, and community gatherings. Pandan Festival Town Plaza The historic center of Mapandan's community life and civic gatherings. Town Plaza Agriculture Rice fields and farmland across Mapandan's countryside — the agricultural heart of the municipality. Agriculture Kasaysayan Ang Mapandan sa mga taon 1887–1909 Pagkakatatag at Maagang Pamamahala From southern barrios of Mangaldan to an independent pueblo—and back again. Mapandan’s first two decades were defined by the courage of its founders, the fragility of a new town, and the determination to rise again. Basahin pa Before 1887: Southern barrios of Mangaldan Before Mapandan existed as an independent pueblo, the area belonged to Mangaldan. The future municipality consisted of southern communities including Payapay, Baloling, Apaya and Amanoaoac. The movement toward establishing a separate town was initiated by ten local leaders: Antonio Morales, Sabino Prado, Andres Bongato, Ambrosio Calimlim, Valeriano Tamondong, Tomas Aquino, Fulgencio Nato, Filomeno Sarmiento, Jose Lalas, and Florencio Datuin. December 28, 1887: Mapandan becomes a pueblo Mapandan was established as an independent pueblo through Direction General No. 39, Administration Civil No. 169-C, signed by Governor General Emilio Bravo. The new pueblo was initially composed of the southern barrios of Mangaldan: Payapay, Baloling, Apaya and Amanoaoac. The first town center: Torres The first center of the new pueblo was in what is now Barangay Torres. The area had abundant pandan plants and was associated with a church where Fr. Jose Torres served as parish priest. However, the location proved inconvenient—too close to the southern boundary and too far from communities to the north. The center was eventually transferred to an area that had previously been a sitio of Apaya. Much of the land in the new Poblacion was owned by the Aquino family. Leon Hilario Aquino encouraged settlement by subdividing land into uniform lots and making them available to families. 1903: The epidemic An epidemic severely affected Mapandan, causing major population depletion, residents leaving the town, declining municipal resources, and a financial crisis. The 1903 census recorded Mapandan’s population at 4,198. 1905–1908: Return to Mangaldan Because of the population and financial problems caused by the epidemic, Mapandan was temporarily returned to its mother municipality, Mangaldan. 1909: Restoration Mapandan was formally re-established as a municipality under Executive Order No. 10, signed by Governor General James F. Smith. 1910s–1940s Paglago ng Agrikultura at Panahon ng Digmaan After its restoration, Mapandan developed as a predominantly agricultural community. Farming remained central to the local economy, with rice becoming the municipality’s principal crop. The decades ahead would bring war, occupation, and the beginning of reconstruction. Basahin pa Agricultural foundations Rice became the municipality’s principal crop and livestock raising developed as an important secondary livelihood. The municipality’s current seal still reflects these agricultural foundations through its rice, cattle, chicken and hog imagery. 1940s: War, occupation and rebuilding The Second World War interrupted the development of communities across Pangasinan. In the postwar years, Mapandan’s communities entered a period of reconstruction and social and economic change. The decades following the war also brought changes in landholding, agriculture, education and local community organization. 1940s–1970s Pag-unlad ng Komunidad Pagkatapos ng Digmaan After the war, Mapandan’s communities began to take shape. New barangays were formed, land ownership changed hands, and the municipality entered a period of organized community development. Basahin pa Barangays begin taking shape Instead of only telling municipal history, the history of how Mapandan’s communities formed tells an equally important story. Sta. Maria — Formerly part of Luyan, developed from former hacienda land. Tenants gained opportunities to own the land they had been farming after the war. It became a separate barrio in 1965. Golden — Formerly Amanoaoac North, a sitio of Amanoaoac. Its name was associated with the Golden Distillery, which operated after liberation. Golden became a separate barangay in 1967. Torres — The first seat of Mapandan, which once contained several sitios that later developed into separate barangays. 1967–1973: Community development Golden was officially approved as a separate barangay in 1967. The community then underwent substantial development including road improvement, waterworks, school construction, sports facilities, cooperative organization, agricultural training, and sanitation programs. 1972 — Golden was recognized as a SEATO/PACD Model Village, receiving a national-level award presented in Malacañang on September 8, 1972. 1972–1973 — Coral became a barangay through Municipal Council Resolution No. 87 (May 4, 1972), Provincial Board Resolution No. 155 (August 10, 1972), and Proclamation No. 11 (April 25, 1973), followed by a special election for barangay officials on May 6, 1973. 1980s–2001 Modernization Mapandan’s population grew substantially, its services expanded, and infrastructure developed. The municipality moved from historical survival toward economic growth. Read more Population growth Mapandan’s population grew steadily through the second half of the 20th century: 20,094 in 1980, 25,622 in 1990, and 30,775 in 2000. Infrastructure and services The municipality expanded roads, schools, health facilities, and public services. Community organizations grew alongside the population. 2002–2024 Pag-unlad sa ika-21 Siglo From a new municipal classification to healthcare expansion and digital government—Mapandan enters the 21st century with growing services, cultural pride, and a more connected community. Read more 2002: A new municipal classification Mapandan was elevated to a third-class municipality. The municipality credits then-Mayor Jose Ferdinand Z. Calimlim Jr. with spearheading income and revenue-generation strategies that contributed to the municipality’s elevation. 2010s: Celebrating the Pandan heritage The Pandan Festival developed into an important annual celebration of Mapandan’s identity, culture and community. The 9th Pandan Festival was held alongside the town fiesta from March 11–19, 2018. 2017–2018: Early digital government efforts The municipal government began developing an online presence that made government information, public notices, disaster information and community announcements accessible through the web. 2022–2024: Expanding healthcare access National health infrastructure funding supported the development of the Mapandan Super Health Center. The 2022 General Appropriations Act included ₱6.5 million for the project. Its first phase was inaugurated on March 15, 2024, expanding access to laboratory, dental and primary healthcare services for residents of Mapandan and nearby communities. 2020s: Government services go digital Mapandan’s government information infrastructure increasingly incorporates digital channels, including information and access guidance for the national eGovPH platform. 2024: Mapandan today More than 130 years after its establishment as a pueblo, Mapandan is a 15-barangay municipality with a population of 38,228. Its history has been shaped by migration, agriculture, community organization, local government, cultural traditions and continuing investment in public services. ← 1 / 5 → Source: Mayor Karl Vega, “History of Mapandan” — YouTube Sources & Historical Notes Historical accounts drawn from municipal archives, provincial records, and published heritage studies of Pangasinan. Municipality of Mapandan — Municipal Profile Municipality of Mapandan — Physical Characteristics Philippine Statistics Authority — Mapandan PSGC Philippine News Agency — Super Health Center Inauguration Paglago ng Populasyon Ang Mapandan sa pamamagitan ng senso Populasyon ayon sa taon ng census Year Population 1903 4,198 1918 6,049 1939 7,286 1948 9,836 1960 13,065 1970 16,653 1980 20,094 1990 25,622 2000 30,775 2010 34,439 2020 38,058 2024 38,228 Source: Philippine Statistics Authority, Census of Population (1903–2024) About the Project Ano ang Better Mapandan? Better Mapandan is an independent civic transparency portal built and maintained by volunteers. It is part of the BetterGov.ph initiative to create open, accessible civic information websites for Philippine municipalities. Aming Misyon To make government information accessible, understandable, and actionable for every Mapandan resident. We believe that open data strengthens democracy and empowers communities to participate meaningfully in local governance. Kung Paano Ito Gumagana We compile publicly available government data — from COA audit reports, PSA census data, municipal disclosures, and provincial issuances — into a single, easy-to-navigate website. Every piece of information is sourced and attributed. Open Source The source code is publicly available. Developers can contribute, audit, and improve the platform. View on GitHub → Independent Ang Better Mapandan ay isang independent na civic transparency portal. Ito ay hindi opisyal na website ng pamahalaan at hindi kaakibat, ineendorso, o pinapatakbo ng Munisipalidad ng Mapandan o ng anumang ahensiya ng pamahalaan. Pinapatakbo ng mga Boluntaryo Built and maintained entirely by volunteers. No government funding is used. Cost to the people of Mapandan: ₱0. Contribute Makilahok Better Mapandan thrives on community participation. Here's how you can help: Iulat ang Maliwang Impormasyon Spotted an error? Help us keep the data accurate by reporting mistakes. Report an error → Mag-contribute ng Code Developers can contribute features, fix bugs, or improve accessibility on GitHub. Fork on GitHub → I-verify ang Datos Help verify government information by cross-referencing with official sources. Submit verification → Ibahagi sa mga Residente Spread the word about Better Mapandan so more residents can access government information. Disclaimer Mahalagang Paunawa Ang Better Mapandan ay isang independent na civic transparency portal. Ito ay hindi opisyal na website ng pamahalaan at hindi kaakibat, ineendorso, o pinapatakbo ng Munisipalidad ng Mapandan o ng anumang ahensiya ng pamahalaan. Information presented on this site is compiled from publicly available government sources and community research. While we strive for accuracy, we cannot guarantee the completeness or timeliness of all data. For official government information, please visit mapandan.gov.ph or contact the municipal government directly.

View full transparency dashboard → Ikatlong Klase na Bayan · Rehiyon I Isang bayang palayan sa ikatlong distrito ng Pangasinan Matatagpuan ang Mapandan sa Ikatlong Kongresonal na Distrito ng Pangasinan, hangganan ng San Jacinto sa hilaga, Mangaldan sa hilagang-kanluran, Manaoag sa silangan, at Santa Barbara sa timog. Sakop nito ang 32.92 square kilometro, kung saan halos tatlo sa apat na bahagi ng lupain ay suportado ang agrikultura — pangunahin ang palay, kasama ang mais, hayop, at mga panahong gulay. Ang pamahalaang bayan ay gumagana sa ilalim ng tagline “Kaakibat niyo ang Aktibo at Responsableng Liderato.” 01 Itinatag noong Dis. 28, 1887 Hiwalay sa Mangaldan bilang isang independenteng pueblo sa ilalim ni Heneral Gobernador Emilio Bravo, pinamunuan ng sampung lokal na lider kabilang si Antonio Morales, Sabino Prado, at Andres Bongato. 02 Muling itinatag noong 1909 Isang matinding epidemya ang nagpilit sa pansamantalang pagsasama muli sa Mangaldan. Ang buong kasarinlan ay naibalik sa pamamagitan ng Executive Order Blg. 10 ni Heneral Gobernador James F. Smith. 03 Puso ng Agrikultura Humigit-kumulang 75% ng 30 km² ng munisipalidad ay inilaan para sa produksyon ng lowland crop, hayop, at pag-aalaga ng manok. Pamumuno Kasalukuyang nakaupo Hon. title: Accessibility Statement — BetterMapandan.org
description: Accessibility commitment and standards for the Better Mapandan civic transparency portal.
body: Support Accessibility Statement Our commitment to making government information accessible to all residents. Our commitment Better Mapandan is committed to ensuring digital accessibility for people with disabilities. We continually improve the user experience for everyone and apply the relevant accessibility standards. Conformance Status We aim to conform to the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 at the AA level. These guidelines explain how to make web content more accessible for people with disabilities. Measures Taken We have implemented the following accessibility features across the site: Semantic HTML structure Skip-to-content navigation link Visible focus indicators Sufficient color contrast (4.5:1 minimum) Keyboard-accessible navigation Screen-reader-friendly labels Descriptive link text Proper heading hierarchy Accessibility features Keyboard Navigation All interactive elements are accessible via keyboard. Use Tab to move between elements, Enter to activate links and buttons, and Escape to close overlays. Screen Readers The site uses semantic HTML, ARIA labels, and proper heading hierarchy to ensure screen readers can navigate the content effectively. Color & Contrast All text meets WCAG AA contrast requirements. Information is never conveyed through color alone — icons, labels, and text are always provided alongside color coding. Text Resizing The site uses relative units (rem, em) for text sizing. Users can resize text up to 200% without loss of content or functionality. Forms All form inputs are associated with labels. Error messages are descriptive and programmatically associated with the relevant input fields. Tables Data tables include proper header associations ( <th scope> ), captions where appropriate, and are responsive on mobile devices. Known limitations We are aware of the following accessibility limitations and are working to address them: PDF documents: Some linked government documents (COA reports, provincial issuances) may not be fully accessible. We provide HTML summaries where possible. Interactive maps: The Leaflet map is navigable via keyboard but may present challenges for screen reader users. We provide alternative text descriptions and a data table fallback. Third-party content: Embedded content from external government websites may not meet the same accessibility standards. Feedback We welcome your feedback on the accessibility of Better Mapandan. If you encounter accessibility barriers, please let us know: Report an Issue Use our reporting form to describe the accessibility issue, the page URL, and your browser/device information. Report accessibility issue → GitHub Issues Developers can file accessibility issues directly on our GitHub repository. Open GitHub issue →

No. Ang Better Mapandan ay isang independent na civic transparency portal. Ito ay hindi opisyal na website ng pamahalaan at hindi kaakibat, ineendorso, o pinapatakbo ng Munisipalidad ng Mapandan o ng anumang ahensiya ng pamahalaan. For official information, visit mapandan.gov.ph . How is this project funded? Better Mapandan is entirely volunteer-run and uses no government funding. The cost to the people of Mapandan is ₱0. Hosting and domain costs are covered by the BetterGov.ph initiative. Where does the data come from? All data is compiled from publicly available government sources: COA audit reports, PSA census data, DILG disclosures, BLGF treasury data, provincial issuances, and municipal announcements. Every source is attributed on the page where the data appears. How do I report incorrect information? Visit our Report Incorrect Information page. Provide the page URL, the specific error, and the correct information if known. Our volunteers will review and update the data. Services Government services How do I get a birth certificate? Visit the Municipal Civil Registrar (MCR) at the 1st Floor, Main Municipal Building, Poblacion. Bring a valid ID and the required fee. Processing time is typically 3–5 working days. See the full requirements on the Birth Certificate service page . How do I apply for a business permit? Visit the Municipal Treasurer's Office (MTO) with your DTI/SEC registration, barangay clearance, and other required documents. New permits are processed in 3–5 working days. See the Business Permit service page for full details. How do I get a building permit? Apply through the Municipal Engineering Office (MEO). Building permits require a zoning clearance, architectural plans, and structural plans. Processing takes 10–15 working days. See the Building Permit service page . How do I request a barangay clearance? Visit your barangay hall with a valid ID. Barangay clearances are typically issued the same day. This is often a prerequisite for other government transactions. Data & Transparency Data questions What does "Placeholder" mean on data? Some data is marked as "Placeholder" when the exact figure is not yet available from official sources. We use reasonable estimates based on available data and clearly mark these so residents know the difference between verified and estimated figures. How often is the data updated? Each data section includes a "Last updated" timestamp. Major updates happen when new COA audit reports, PSA census data, or municipal financial disclosures become available. The site is continuously improved by volunteers. Can I download the data? Yes. The Statistics page includes CSV download options for chart data. The Transparency page provides links to source documents. All data is publicly available and free to reuse under open data principles. How can I verify the data myself? Every data section includes a source attribution and, where available, a link to the original document. You can cross-reference with official sources like the COA website, PSA, or the municipal government directly. Contact Still have questions? For government services Contact the relevant office directly. See the Government Directory for phone numbers and email addresses. For this website Report issues, suggest improvements, or contribute on GitHub . For data corrections, use the Report Incorrect Information form.

title: Privacy Policy — BetterMapandan.org
description: Privacy policy for the Better Mapandan civic transparency portal.
body: Legal Privacy Policy How we handle data on the Better Mapandan civic transparency portal. Overview Ang Better Mapandan ay isang independent na civic transparency portal. Ito ay hindi opisyal na website ng pamahalaan at hindi kaakibat, ineendorso, o pinapatakbo ng Munisipalidad ng Mapandan o ng anumang ahensiya ng pamahalaan. We collect minimal data and are committed to protecting your privacy. Information We Collect Automatically collected: When you visit Better Mapandan, our hosting provider (GitHub Pages) may collect standard web server logs including your IP address, browser type, referring URL, and pages visited. This is standard server operation and is not used to identify individual visitors. Search queries: The search functionality runs entirely in your browser. Your search queries are never sent to a server or stored. Language preference: If you use the language switcher (when available), your preference is stored locally in your browser and is never transmitted to us. How We Use Information We do not use, sell, or share personal information. Server logs are used only for maintaining the website and understanding usage patterns in aggregate. Cookies Better Mapandan does not use cookies. The language preference is stored using localStorage , which is a browser-only storage mechanism and is not transmitted to any server. Third-Party Services The site loads the following external resources: Google Fonts (fonts.googleapis.com) — for font loading Open-Meteo API (open-meteo.com) — for weather data (loaded only on the homepage) Leaflet / OpenStreetMap — for the interactive map (loaded only on the homepage) These services have their own privacy policies. We do not share any personal data with them. Data Sources All government data presented on this site is compiled from publicly available official sources. This data is already public and is presented here for informational purposes. Changes to This Policy This privacy policy may be updated from time to time. Changes will be posted on this page with an updated date. Contact For privacy-related inquiries, please open an issue on our GitHub repository or use the report form .

Statutory Pondong Panspesyal na Edukasyon (SEF) Financed through a 1% tax levy on assessed real property values under Section 235 of R.A. 7160. Co-administered by the Municipal School Board. title: Aics
body: Serbisyong Panlipunan — Mga ID at Sertipikasyon Tulong sa AICS Mag-apply para sa Assistance to Individual sa Crisis Situations (AICS) sa Mapandan. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "GovernmentService", "name": "Tulong sa AICS", "description": "Ang Assistance to Individuals in Crisis Situations (AICS) ay isang programa ng pamahalaan na nagbibigay ng tulong pinansyal sa mga indibidwal at pamilya na nahaharap sa mga emergency.", "provider": { "@type": "GovernmentOrganization", "name": "Municipality of Mapandan", "address": { "@type": "PostalAddress", "addressLocality": "Mapandan", "addressRegion": "Pangasinan", "addressCountry": "PH" } }, "serviceType": "Serbisyong Panlipunan — Mga ID at Sertipikasyon", "areaServed": { "@type": "Place", "name": "Mapandan, Pangasinan, Philippines" } } Paglalarawan Assistance to Individuals in Crisis Situations (AICS) is a government program that provides financial assistance to individuals and families facing emergencies such as medical crises, bereavement, or other unforeseen circumstances. In Mapandan, AICS assistance is administered by the Municipal Social Welfare and Development Office (MSWDO) in coordination with the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD). Mga Kinakailangan Barangay certification stating the resident’s crisis situation Medical certificate (for medical-related assistance) Death certificate (for burial assistance) Valid government-issued ID Case study or social worker assessment Prosedura Secure a barangay certification from your barangay captain or kagawad. Gather all required documents (medical certificate, death certificate, etc.). Visit the MSWDO office and submit your application with supporting documents. Wait for the social worker’s assessment and case study. Receive financial assistance upon approval of your application. Saklaw ang standard registration (₱115), registration ng mga magulang na hindi kasal (₱215), hospital registration (₱100), at late registration (₱315–₱1,015).", "provider": { "@type": "GovernmentOrganization", "name": "Municipality of Mapandan", "address": { "@type": "PostalAddress", "addressLocality": "Mapandan", "addressRegion": "Pangasinan", "addressCountry": "PH" } }, "serviceType": "Civil Registry at mga Vital Record", "areaServed": { "@type": "Place", "name": "Mapandan, Pangasinan, Philippines" } } Paglalarawan A birth certificate is a vital record that serves as proof of identity, age, and Filipino citizenship. title: Building Permit
body: Gusali, Engineering, at Zoning Building Permit Kumuha ng building permit mula sa Mapandan MEO. Simple: 3 araw, Complex: 7 araw, Highly Technical: 20 araw ayon sa RA 11032. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "GovernmentService", "name": "Building Permit", "description": "Ang building permit ay kinakailangan sa ilalim ng National Building Code (PD 1096) at RA 11032. Oras ng pagproseso: Simple — 3 working days, Complex — 7 working days, Highly Technical — 20 working days.", "provider": { "@type": "GovernmentOrganization", "name": "Municipality of Mapandan", "address": { "@type": "PostalAddress", "addressLocality": "Mapandan", "addressRegion": "Pangasinan", "addressCountry": "PH" } }, "serviceType": "Gusali, Engineering, at Zoning", "areaServed": { "@type": "Place", "name": "Mapandan, Pangasinan, Philippines" } } Paglalarawan A building permit is a legal requirement under the National Building Code of the Philippines (PD 1096) for any construction, renovation, alteration, or demolition of a building or structure. The Municipal Engineering Office (MEO) of Mapandan reviews and issues building permits after ensuring compliance with safety standards, zoning, and structural requirements. Mga Kinakailangan Plans duly signed & sealed by licensed professionals Certified true copy of Tax Declaration (from Assessor Office) Xerox copy of land title (from Register of Deeds) Community Tax Certificate (from Treasury Office) Latest Tax receipts (from Treasury Office) Electrical & Sanitary permit (from Municipal Health Office) Confirmation of adjoining lot owners Certification from Barangay Captain Application for locational clearance (from Zoning Office) 2 Affidavits (from Notary Public) Affidavit of consent if not lot owner (from Notary Public) Fire Safety clearance (from BFP Office) Affidavit of adjoining lot owners Prosedura Obtain a zoning clearance from the MPDC / Zoning Office. Prepare architectural and structural plans signed by licensed professionals. Submit all documents to the Municipal Engineering Office (MEO) for review. Pay the building permit fees at the Municipal Treasurer’s Office. Receive the approved building permit after technical evaluation. title: Business Permit
body: Pagpapasyal at Lisensya ng Negosyo Bagong Business Permit Mag-apply para sa bagong business permit sa BPLO sa Mapandan. Kabilang ang endorsement sa Engineering, MPDC, RHU, at BFP. { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "GovernmentService", "name": "Bagong Business Permit", "description": "Ang business permit ay kinakailangan para sa lahat ng indibidwal o entity na nagpaplanong mag-operate ng negosyo sa loob ng Bayan ng Mapandan.", "provider": { "@type": "GovernmentOrganization", "name": "Municipality of Mapandan", "address": { "@type": "PostalAddress", "addressLocality": "Mapandan", "addressRegion": "Pangasinan", "addressCountry": "PH" } }, "serviceType": "Pagpapasyal at Lisensya ng Negosyo", "areaServed": { "@type": "Place", "name": "Mapandan, Pangasinan, Philippines" } } Paglalarawan A business permit is required for all individuals or entities intending to operate a commercial business within the Municipality of Mapandan. This permit is issued after compliance with documentary and safety requirements and upon payment of applicable fees. Mga Kinakailangan Filled up UNIFIED Form / Community Tax Certificate (from BPLO/Treasury Office) DTI/SEC/CDA Registration (from DTI/SEC/CDA Office or Online Application) BIR COR, if available (from RDO Calasiao) Barangay Clearance (System Integrated) Prosedura Fill up the UNIFIED form and submit necessary requirements for verification (10 min). BPLO encodes data into the e-BPLS System. BPLO endorses applicant to various offices: Engineering (Occupancy Certificate), MPDC (Zoning Certificate), RHU (Health Certificate & Sanitary Permit), BFP (Fire Safety Inspection Certificate) (44 min). Pay fees and charges at the Treasury Office. Proceed to the Mayor's Office for issuance of Business Permit. Claim business plate and sticker at the Treasury Office (10 min). Mga Detalye ng Serbisyo Opisyo na May Pananagutan: Business Permit and Licensing Office (BPLO) Klasipikasyon: Simple Paraan: in-person Oras ng Pagproseso: ~1 hour (10 min encoding + 44 min endorsement + 10 min pay & claim) Bayad: Mayor's Permit (₱500–₱1,000) + Business Plate & Sticker (₱250) + Weights & Measure (₱100–200) + Storage Fee (₱550) + Garbage Fee (₱800–₱1,200) Saan Mag-aapply: 1st Floor, Main Municipal Building, Poblacion Contact: (075) 696-0831 / 0998-577-3164 Pinagmulan: Mapandan Citizen’s Charter Huling Na-update: August 2025 Iulat ang maling impormasyon Nascanned na Dokumento Nascanned na pahina mula sa opisyal na Mapandan Citizen's Charter na naglilista ng mga kinakailangan, bayad, oras ng pagproseso, at mga staff na may pananagutan para sa serbisyo.
